sentences.text:
This second appeal is filed by the appellant challenging the judgment and decree dated 08.10.2015,
passed in R.A.No.40/2013 by the Senior Civil Judge & JMFC, Harapanahalli, confirming the judgment and decree dated 19.07.2012, passed in O.S.No.236/2007 by the Civil Judge,
Harapanahalli.
For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the trial Court.

The appellant is the defendant No.1; respondent No.1 is the plaintiff; respondents No.2 to 24 are defendants No.2 to 24.
3.

The brief facts leading rise to filing of this appeal are as under:
It is the case of the plaintiff that the plaintiff is the son of Budji Badesab, S/o Late Dadasab and the defendants are the children and grandchildren of Late Badesab.

Said Badesab had 8 children, namely, Imam Bi, Gani Sab, Dadesab, Mariyan Bi,
Hussain Sab, Alla Bakash, Mahaboob Sab and Mustafa.
Out of them, Imam Bi, Gane Sab and Dade Sab are no more.

Late Budji Badesab and his sons got divided their properties through registered partition deed dated 07.02.1981, and in the partition,
property worth about Rs.15,000/- was given to Late Badesab and property worth Mehaboob Sab vs Budji Mustafa on 11 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125349176/
4 about Rs.1,500/- each was given to plaintiff and other male sons of Late Badesab.

Plaintiff's father and his sons are the joint owners of property measuring 7.14 acres in Sy.No.2 of Adavihalli Village and out of the said property, an extent of 4.14 acres were partitioned and the remaining 3 acres was not partitioned among the joint owners.
As per the partition deed, 'A' schedule property measuring 6.20 acres and the land in Sy.No.236/A was allotted to the father of the plaintiff.
The said property is in joint possession of the plaintiff and other family members.
After the death of father of plaintiff, the plaintiff has succeeded to the suit schedule properties.
Plaintiff is the absolute owner of the suit schedule property under partition deed dated 07.02.1981.
Defendants No.22 and 23 have acquired the property bearing Sy.No.2 for public purpose.
The plaintiff is entitled for compensation of his share.
The plaintiff came to know that the defendant No.1 has taken the compensation amount towards the entire 7.14 acres.
Thereafter, the plaintiff got issued legal notice to defendants No.22 and 23.
It is learnt by the plaintiff that defendant No.1 has created the sale deed showing that NC: 2023:KHC:37038 the plaintiff has sold his share of land measuring 2.07 acres in favour of defendant No.1.
The sale deed is created by defendant No.1.
Hence cause of action arose for the plaintiff to file the suit for partition and separate possession and declaration of sale deed as null and void.

4. Defendant No.1 filed written statement denying the averments made in the plaint and contended that the defendant No.1 is the absolute owner of the property measuring 2.07 acres in Sy.No.2 and the property measuring 1.72 acres in Sy.No.193 and house bearing No.582 under registered partition deed dated 07.02.1981.
On 16.01.1984, the plaintiff had sold his share in Sy.No.2 in favour of defendant No.1 through registered sale deed.
On the strength of the registered sale deed, the name of defendant No.1 was entered in the revenue records.
The Government has acquired the land bearing Sy.No.2 as per law.
Hence defendant No.1 prays to dismiss the suit.

5. Defendants No.22 and 23 filed written statement contending that they have already paid the compensation NC: 2023:KHC:37038 for acquisition of lands and the plaintiff can recover the said amount from defendant No.1 who has withdrawn the compensation amount and suit is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties and prayed to dismiss the suit against defendants No.22 and 23.
6.

The Trial Court, on the basis of the above said pleadings, framed the following issues:
1) Whether the plaintiff proves that the property bearing Sy. No.2 of 3 acre are not portioned between the plaintiff and defendants on 07.02.1981?
2) Whether the plaintiff proves that sale deed dated 16.01.1984 is forged, concocted and created by defendant No.1 and not binding on plaintiff?

Mehaboob Sab vs Budji Mustafa on 11 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125349176/
5 3) Whether plaintiff proves that the suit properties are joint possession of plaintiff and defendant No.1 to 21?
4) Whether defendant No.1 proves that he has purchased the property bearing Sy.No.2 of 2.07 acres through the registered sale deed dated 07.02.1982 after partition?
5) Whether the defendant No.22 and 23 proves that suit is bad for non joinder of necessary parties?

NC: 2023:KHC:37038 6) Whether the defendant No.22 and 23 proves that this Court has no jurisdiction to try the case?
7) Whether the plaintiff is entitled the relief as claimed in the plaint?
8) What order or decree?
7. In order to prove the case of the plaintiff, the plaintiff examined himself as PW-1 and got examined two witnesses as PW-2 & PW-3 and got marked 24 documents as Exs.P1 to P24.

Defendant No.1 examined himself as DW-1; got examined two witnesses as DW-2 & DW-3; and on behalf of defendants No.22 and 23, the GPA holder was examined as DW-4 and got marked 5 documents as Exs.D1 to D5.

The trial Court after considering the oral and documentary evidence of the parties, answered issue Nos.1, 2 and 7 in affirmative; issue No.3 partly in affirmative and issue Nos.4 and 5 in negative and consequently decreed the suit with costs.
It is declared that the plaintiff is entitled for compensation amount in respect of his share of 2.07 acres in Sy.No.2 of Adavihalli Village from defendants No.1, 22 and 23.

It is further - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:37038 ordered that the plaintiff is entitled for 2/14th share in Sy.No.2 measuring 3 acres and 2/14th share in 6.20 acres in Sy.No.236/A by metes and bounds and that plaintiff is entitled for compensation amount in respect of 2/14th share in Sy.No.2 of 3 acres at Adavihalli Village from defendants No.22 and 23.
It is further declared that th sale deed dated 16.01.1981, is not binding on the plaintiff.
8. The defendant No.1 aggrieved by the judgment and preliminary decree passed in the above said suit, filed an appeal in R.A.No.40/2013.

The First Appellate Court, after hearing the parties, has framed the following points for consideration:
1) Whether the trial Court judge is right in decreeing the suit?
2) Whether the interference of this Court is necessary?
3) What order?

6 9.

The First Appellate Court, on re-appreciating the oral and documentary evidence, answered point No.1 in affirmative and point No.2 in negative and consequently - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:37038 dismissed the appeal filed by the defendant No.1, confirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court.
The defendant No.1, aggrieved by the judgments and decrees passed by the courts below, has filed this second appeal.

10. Heard learned counsel for defendant No.1.
11.
Learned counsel for defendant No.1 submits that the plaintiff has executed a registered sale deed in favour of defendant No.1 on 16.01.1984.
He submits that there is a presumption in regard to the execution of the registered documents.
The courts below have committed an error in not drawing the presumption.
He further submits that the plaintiff delivered possession of the suit schedule properties in favour of defendant No.1.

On the strength of the registered sale deed, the name of defendant No.1 was entered in the revenue records and defendant No.1 has produced the revenue records to establish his possession over the suit schedule property.
He further submits that the Karnataka Housing Board has - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:37038 acquired the suit land and surrounding lands and defendant No.1 has withdrawn the compensation amount.
Hence he submits that the courts below have not properly considered the pleadings and the oral and documentary evidence.
Hence he submits that the courts below have committed an error in passing the impugned judgments.
On these grounds prays to allow the appeal.

12. Perused the records and considered the submissions of learned counsel for defendant No.1.
13.
It is the case of the plaintiff that the suit properties were owned and possessed by Badesab.
There was partition between Badesab and his children and the said partition was reduced into writing and it is registered on 07.02.1981.
In the said partition, the suit schedule properties were fallen to the share of father of plaintiff and after his death, the plaintiff succeeded to the suit schedule properties.
Further, it is the case of the plaintiff that the Karnataka Housing Board had acquired the said lands.

The plaintiff approached the Karnataka Housing Board for - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:37038 release of compensation amount, but the plaintiff came to know that the defendant No.1 had withdrawn the compensation amount on the ground that plaintiff had executed the registered sale deed in favour of defendant No.1 on 16.01.1984.

The plaintiff immediately issued a legal notice to defendants No.22 and 23 stating that the defendant No.1 got created the registered sale deed dated 16.01.1984, and requested not to release the compensation amount.

7 order to substantiate his case, examined himself as PW-1.

sentences.text: He has reiterated the plaint averments in the examination-in- chief.
He has denied the execution of registered sale deed dated 16.01.1984 and also denied his signature on the alleged registered sale deed.
The plaintiff has produced records to show that the said property was originally owned by Badesab and thereafter there was a partition between Badesab and his sons.
In the said partition, the suit properties were fallen to the share of plaintiff's father.

Defendant No.1 has not denied about the partition that took place between Badesab and his sons on 07.02.1981 - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:37038 and also that the suit schedule properties were fallen to the share of plaintiff's father.
14. It is the case of the defendant No.1, that plaintiff had executed registered sale deed in respect of the suit schedule properties in his favour.
Plaintiff has denied the execution of registered sale deed.
Hence, the burden is on the defendant No.1 to prove that the plaintiff had executed the registered sale deed.
Further, the plaintiff had also denied his signature on the alleged registered sale deed.
Defendant No.1 has not produced the original registered sale deed.
On the contrary, has produced the certified copy of the registered sale deed.
Further, the defendant No.1 has not taken any steps to prove the signature of plaintiff on the registered sale deed dated 16.01.1084.

When the plaintiff has specifically denied his signature on the alleged registered sale deed, and also execution, the burden is cast upon the defendant No.1 to prove the contents as well as the signature of plaintiff on the registered sale deed.
Further, defendant No.1 has - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:37038 withheld the original registered sale deed.
The said document goes to the root of the case.
Hence, in view of non-production of original registered sale deed, an adverse inference has to be drawn against defendant No.1 under Section 114(g) of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
Defendant No.1 has failed to establish that the plaintiff had executed the registered sale deed in his favour.

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of DHANI RAM (DIED)
THROUGH LRS. & ORS. VS. SHIV SINGH, disposed on 06.10.2023, wherein it is held that, "mere registration would not sanctify a document by attaching to it an irrebuttable presumption of genuineness".

DHANI RAM (DIED)
THROUGH LRS. & ORS. VS. SHIV SINGH
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court that the contention of defendant No.1 that the sale deed is registered, a presumption can be drawn, does not hold water.

15. The courts below have concurrently recorded a finding of fact against the defendant No.1 holding that defendant No.1 has failed to prove that the plaintiff had - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:37038 executed a registered sale deed in favour of defendant No.1 and defendant No.1 became the absolute owner on the strength of the registered sale deed dated 16.01.1984.
Both the courts below were justified in passing the impugned judgments and decrees.

I do not find any Mehaboob Sab vs Budji Mustafa on 11 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125349176/
8 grounds to interfere with the impugned judgments and decrees.
I do not find any substantial question of law that arise for consideration in this appeal.

16. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The appeal is dismissed.
The judgments and decrees passed by the courts below are confirmed.
No order as to the costs.

In view of dismissal of the appeal,
 pending I.As., if any, do not arise for consideration and are accordingly disposed of.
